Steve Battle (born c. 1979) is an American former college football wide receiver who played at Valley City State University (VCSU) from 1999 to 2002. He is regarded as one of the most accomplished receivers in school history and is a member of the VCSU Vikings Hall of Fame.
A three-time NAIA All-American, Battle set multiple program records and helped lead Valley City State to a 32–9 record and two NAIA playoff appearances during his collegiate career. Following college, he participated in training camp with the St. Louis Rams of the National Football League (NFL).
College career
Battle arrived at Valley City State University in 1999 and became one of the most productive receivers in the NAIA.
He had a breakout sophomore season in 2000, recording 18 total touchdowns, earning Second-Team NAIA All-American honors and First-Team All-Conference recognition.
He repeated as a Second-Team All-American and First-Team All-Conference selection in 2001. As a senior in 2002, Battle was named the Most Valuable Graduating Senior in the conference and earned NAIA Honorable Mention All-American recognition.
During Battle's four-year career, VCSU went 32–9, made two NAIA playoff appearances, and established itself as one of the top programs in the region.
School records
As of 2025, Battle continues to hold multiple Valley City State career and single-game records:
* Career total touchdowns: 55
* Career receptions: 182
* Career receiving yards: 3,337
* Career receiving touchdowns: 48
* Single-game receiving yards: 234
Professional career
After going undrafted in 2003, Battle earned a tryout opportunity with the St. Louis Rams and joined the team for rookie and veteran training camp.
The Fargo-Moorhead Forum reported that Battle impressed coaches with his speed and playmaking ability as he attempted to earn a roster position during the preseason. He was later released as part of the team's roster cuts.
Legacy
Battle is widely regarded as one of the greatest offensive players in VCSU history and remains one of only a few Viking football players to earn three All-American honors. He was inducted into the VCSU Vikings Hall of Fame for his outstanding contributions and record-setting career.
